source.name: Arrow keys in a tab list must move keyboard focus to the newly selected tab

journey.title: Walk the settings tabs with arrow keys
journey.goal: Each arrow press selects and focuses the next tab

functionalJourney.title: Switch settings sections with the mouse
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a tab shows its panel

guards.title: Tab from the active tab into its panel
guards.goal: Tab leaves the tab list for the active panel

plan.root_cause: The ArrowRight keydown handler activates the next tab but does not move focus to it, causing focus to remain on the previously activated tab (which is blurred) or fall back to the body, breaking expected keyboard navigation.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the _keydown method in js/src/tab.js to focus the newly activated tab after calling show(), ensuring arrow key navigation moves focus as required by ARIA authoring practices.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft keys will now move focus to the adjacent tab and update its aria-selected attribute, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability and 2.4.3 focus order for the tablist.
functional_risks: Focus may be set before a fade transition completes, but the element remains focusable and accessible.
If the tab list were to include disabled tabs, the filtering logic already excludes them, so no additional risk.
verification_requirements: Pressing ArrowRight from the Account tab should move focus to the Notifications tab and set its aria-selected to true.
Pressing ArrowRight again should move focus to the Billing tab and set its aria-selected to true.
Pressing ArrowLeft should reverse focus movement accordingly.
Focus should never shift to the body or become lost during navigation.
Tab panel visibility should update correctly in sync with the selected tab.
